And these are the conclusions reached by the two ECMM representatives that were present at this meeting with you and Rasula, the HDZ representative, and the chief of police. And this was their conclusion in their report to Sarajevo. "However, they tried to give the impression of good cooperation. It was clear that Muslim and Croatian communities are scared of the Serbian authorities. If this is not solved, it could lead to internal conflicts among the ethnic groups." Mr. Karabeg, in February of 1992 would you say that that was a fair impression of the position in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: There is one final matter, Your Honour. And I'm not going to put it to the witness, but I'm going to state it for the record. And that is Prosecutor's Exhibit 608, which is an order -- a report, rather, by General Talic to the Main Staff of -- in fact, not the Main Staff. To the -- it's a command to the 10th Partisan Division of the 5th Corps. And it was read out to the witness. And it's page 48 of the draft transcript. And I'm referring now, if you go to paragraph 1 of that document, the second paragraph, where it reads "After the march, deploy the units in Sanski Most." And Ms. Fauveau said at page 48, it is not quite clear whether the word "preventing" relates also to the second part of the sentence. The order that General Talic gives after the colon it reads: "With the following task, achieving full control of the territory, preventing inter-ethnic conflicts, setting up roadblocks and securing features of special importance." The position I think of General Talic's Defence is that that means he was ordering the prevention of setting up of roadblocks. Our position is that he was giving an order to set up roadblocks. And I'm going to send this document back to the translation document to have that confirmed. There is a comma in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is more than one comma.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes. There is more than one come match. But certainly with the comma as it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I think you are doing the right thing, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We believe it means what I've just stated. But naturally Ms. Fauveau can take her position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I quite understand the position of Mr. Cayley. But I was referring to the Serbo-Croatian version, and I think General Talic wrote in Serbo-Croatian. And I think in that version, it is quite clear what he wanted to say. Also, there is a report. I think it is 609 Prosecutor's Exhibit where it is also mentioned, and in the English version it is very clear what General Talic wanted to say and that is he wanted to prevent the building of roadblocks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you Madam Fauveau. And I would suggest that you do exactly what you promised to do, because I think it would be important. I'm sure that this document will come up -- or these two documents will come up again and again. So it will be useful to have a proper translation or a second check. Thank you, Mr. Cayley. Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I just have one further mat their wish to inquire into.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when did you -- when were you first visited by the Red Cross? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in July 1992 in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which prison? In Betonirka or in the police prison?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the police prison. In the police prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you state to them how you had been treated by the Serb authorities, to the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell them that you'd been beaten?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. Because I was alone with them, so I was able to tell them that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ask you why you'd been beaten?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say to them?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered that they would always find excuses, not only when they beat me but when they beat the others as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From the Bench side, there are no questions also, which means, Mr. Karabeg, that we come to the end of your testimony. I take this opportunity on behalf of the other two Judges and on behalf of the Tribunal to thank you for having accepted to come here and give evidence. You will be escorted now outside of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Before the witness leaves, Your Honour, I haven't obviously been able to talk to him while he's been giving evidence. But representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor would like to speak with him now he's finished his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If he's finished, he's finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So if I could communicate that to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You will be escorted out of this courtroom, and we wish you a safe journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to thank you and the members of the Trial Chamber for the very correct conduct of the proceedings during my examination as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Karabeg. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before Mr. Ackerman, Madam Fauveau, and Mr. Cayley, before we proceed with the next witness, shall we round up the documentation to make sure that everything has been tendered. I don't think that everything has been tendered. For example, this last document, P802 hasn't as yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: 798, 799, 800, and 801 are four photographs; two from Sanski Most and two from Manjaca. And 802 is this last extract from this book. So if there are no objections, Your Honour, I apply for those to be admitted into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: None other -- none other than the authenticity objections that have been made at the beginning of the case. I don't recall that I have tendered any of the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, exactly. I was coming back to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In the last month or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So there was the whole series of documents starting in the 60s -- or maybe 70 or something like that with regard to the last witness. And with regard to this witness, there's 84 A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. With regard to the last witness -- the previous -- not this last one but the previous one, we had agreed, if you remember, Mr. Ackerman, that I pointed out to you that you had handed us documents, some of which you had made reference to in the course of your cross-examination. Some others you had absolutely ignored. And we had asked you to decide which ones you were tendering -- you were tendering in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I will get that worked out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. We're still waiting for --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: One of the documents with regard to the last witness was rather loudly objected to by Ms. Korner, and I think she wanted to speak maybe some more about it. And that was the transcript of the testimony. And so I will certainly not ask you to admit that until we've both had a chance to make whatever arguments we want to make about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But do discuss this or see to it and come back, because it's the sequence -- numerical sequence which could create problems. Otherwise, I don't foresee any major problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The other thing that I want to tell you, Your Honour, is that -- that I have had an opportunity to spend some time going through the documents that came from Mr. Dzonlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You were supposed to tell us, yes. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And what I'm -- what I'm going to do is I'm going to submit them to CLSS for translation I hope today. I've got them with me. And when they come back, I will then have them marked as exhibits and ask they be put in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Madam Fauveau, with the exception of DT14 or -- do you have any other documents that you would like to tender?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have no other documents and I have no objection to the documents of the Prosecution being tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So that solves the issue of the documentation, of the documents, saving what you still need to come back to us with. The next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour. It does actually follow the order of the new list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I can commit myself, I think, to the last list. I did discuss with my learned friends yesterday swapping them round for internal reasons, but we are going to stick to the original list. And the name of this witness -- can I mention the name? Is he public session? It's Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rajif Begic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Rajif Begic. And my colleague Ms. Richterova will be leading this witness in evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you'll just give me a moment to move my documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, I think we will require -- I think I can say it straight away that we will require the photocopy of the statements that this witness -- the proper ones, the ones which bear his signature and that of Zijad Ibric and Adil Draganovic, because the ones that we have here are just copies -- without a copy of the signature, and I am sure we're going to get to that stage at some point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes. So you -- essentially the statement taken by the Bosnian authorities, you require the original version with the signatures. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we better have it, in any case, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And there are two statements that we have here which I think are the same statements that were -- we exhibited in the other --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We'll need to send them out, Your Honour, to get them copied, but we can do that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, to you, Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we start our business and you start giving your evidence, according to the Rules you are required to enter a solemn declaration that you will tell us the truth and the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Now, the usher will give you the document on which the proper declaration is already written. And may I kindly ask you to read it out and make the solemn declaration aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Begic. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And before we start, I will more or less explain to you the whole layout. I am the President of this Trial Chamber, and I am flanked with the other two Judges that form this Trial Chamber. To my right is Judge Janu from the Czech Republic; to my left is Judge Taya from Japan. I am Judge Agius from Malta. To your right, you see the team for the Prosecution. And the lady next -- nearest to you will be the person from the team of the Prosecution to conduct your examination-in-chief. To your left, you have two rows. The front row, starting with the gentleman and then the young lady and the other gentleman, that's the Defence team for accused Radoslav Brdjanin. The back, there is -- you can see a lady. That lady is the Defence counsel for General Momir Talic. The persons in front of us is the registry team of this Trial Chamber. Now, the procedure to be followed is as follows: You will first be asked questions by the representative -- by counsel for the Prosecution, and that will be followed when they are ready by cross-examination forthcoming first from one Defence team and then from the next Defence team. So having said that, I think we may proceed. Madam Richterova will question you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Ms. Richterova:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: My name is Rajif Begic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born on the 23rd of September, 1967; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were born in the village of Kljevci.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that you are of Bosniak nationality of Islamic faith?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show you a map which has already been tendered into evidence under P757.2. It's the map of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We have enough copies for Defence lawyers and the Judges if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think, Madam Richterova, we can put it on the ELMO. This is a map that we are familiar with. We have seen it again and again and again. So I think Mr. Ackerman doesn't want to see it again. He knows it by heart by now. Yes. Mr. Begic, please look at that map. You're going to be asked by Madam Richterova to point out some places to us. You will have a pointer in your hand, and that's what you'll do. And we can see -- follow what you're pointing at from here, from our monitors. Madam Richterova, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, please can you assist the Court and point at the village of Kljevci and the hamlet in which you lived in 1992.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Kljevci, as situated here, next to the Sana River. And this is the hamlet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the ethnic composition of the village of Kljevci and hamlets which belonged to this village.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: It was mixed. There were hamlets of Serb ethnicity and hamlets of Muslim ethnicity. Starting from Kljevci, in which the majority was Serbs; then there was Kenjari, mostly inhabited by Muslims. Then between Kenjari and Begici, another Serb hamlet. And then the hamlet of Begici, where the majority were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now, I thank you. We can remove the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to direct you back to your village and discuss the events which happened in 1992. Before we start, just briefly can you tell us was life any different in 1992 at the beginning or -- or let us say, the first half of the year 1992 from previous years?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the differences.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992, one could feel political change in town. Our neighbours of Serb ethnicity were setting up checkpoints in front of their hamlets, and we were checked each time we passed through that checkpoint and by their houses. They were not as friendly as before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned these checkpoints. Who was manning these checkpoints? Did you know these people?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did know them. They were local inhabitants of Cosici and other hamlets, and also present were some soldiers who were deployed there by the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned soldiers deployed by the army. Can you be more specific. Which soldiers and which unit did they belong?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew a soldier, Jadranko Palija who was deployed there and they were housed in the school in Kljevci. And from there, they patrolled Kenjari and Begici, the small hamlets there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at that time which unit did they belong?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: From previous conversations with some people, I learnt that it was the 6th Krajina Brigade that had been deployed in the entire area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- apart from discussions, have you received this information from some other sources?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any announcements related to weapons? The time we are talking about is the first half of the year of 1992.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know exactly how much prior to the attack on the village, but at the beginning of May it was already announced on the radio that the inhabitants should hand in their weapons at the closest Serbian checkpoint or military checkpoint. And this was broadcast on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which radio it was?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Radio Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it indicated what would happen to the people or villages which would not comply with that order?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. They threatened to shell the villages and that they wouldn't be able to guarantee the security of the inhabitants if the weapons were not surrendered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any weapons in your hamlet of Begici?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do with these weapons? I will -- excuse me. I will reformulate. What kind of weapons did you have in your village?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I knew of an old hunting rifle owned by a neighbour, and I heard from other neighbours that they had legal pistols which they did surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you own a weapon?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a few moments ago that there was an announcement about handing over weapons before the attack on your village. Let me direct you to this attack. Who attacked your village and when?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: On the 25th of May was the first time that units of the army entered our hamlet. Among them, there were a couple of neighbours from the neighbouring village of Cosici and Stojinovici and several other soldiers whose names I didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who were these soldiers, which unit they belonged?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: They were Serb soldiers from the mentioned unit, the one I mentioned a moment ago, the 6th Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: They were wearing military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe these uniforms, what you remember.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: They were SMB-coloured uniforms, and some had camouflage clothing, also military camouflage clothing on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any insignias on these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Serbian flag on their left arm and some other symbols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that these soldiers arrived to your village around the 25th of May. Tell us what happened after these soldiers arrived.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: You mean the moment they arrived or when they left?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I mean the moment -- when they arrived to your village. They arrived around the 25th of May to your village. What happened after they arrived to your village?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: On that day, they took Ismet Kurbegovic, Begic Sacir, Begic Ismet and they beat them that day on charges that Ismet Kurbegovic owned a sniper rifle, that Sacir Begic was concealing some soldiers in his house, so they beat them up and they searched their houses that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present during these searches?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I was in my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn about what happened in the village?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: My mother was present when they arrived, and I visited these neighbours myself after they -- these others withdrew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else -- you said that they beaten these three men, they searched houses. What else did they do?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: They cursed them. They humiliated them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did they stay in the village?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: One hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did they -- where did they leave then?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Afterwards they withdrew to the checkpoint from which they had come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these soldiers? Did you know names of any of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name some of them.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Cosic Ranko, who was the commander of that checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: They were Serb reservists, not regulars, not regular soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you distinguish between regular and reservist soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, regular soldiers can only be up to 23 or 24, plus minus a couple of years, but they cannot be 40 and over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they left after one hour, and it happened around the 25th of May. Did these soldiers or any other soldiers return to your village at some later stage?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. They came on the next day. They again beat up Ismet Kurbegovic and later on they came on another day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how long -- how long lasted their visits to your village?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: They came twice -- twice before coming again on the 31st of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to direct your attention now to the 31st of May. You said that soldiers arrived again to your village on the 31st of May. What soldiers did arrive that day?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: On the 31st of May, other soldiers came. Not the same ones that came on the 25th, that is, the neighbours, because they were clearing the neighbouring hamlets. So it was -- these were younger soldiers, and I didn't know them nor the neighbours -- they were not neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at that time what kind of soldiers they were? I mean which unit they belonged.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I believe they belonged to the 6th Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why do you believe they belonged to this unit?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Well, on the radio, it was broadcast that the 6th Krajina Brigade was cleaning -- clearing the terrain, the shelling. I believe that they also bore the insignia of the 6th Krajina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these new soldiers arrived on the 31st of May to your village. When did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: They -- in the smaller hamlet of Begici rounded us up at around 3.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when they round you up, where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Then they took us all together, men, women, children, and the elderly, to the other settlement -- hamlet of Begici, where we then joined the other inhabitants of that hamlet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many inhabitants were there approximately?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, some 20 males, women, children - I don't know how many, but maybe approximately 20, 25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you joined the other people in the upper part of Begici there, did you know any of that soldiers? Did you recognise any of that soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I recognised -- some I don't know their names any more. They were of Serbian nationality. They -- we went to school together in Sanski Most. I remember a young man who was a waiter in a cafe in the town. I knew Jadranko Palija, who was at the checkpoint in our hamlet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you gathered -- when the soldiers gathered all inhabitants of your village, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Then they ordered that on one side of the road the children and women congregate and on the other side the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after this separation? What happened to women and what happened to men?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: They ordered the women and children to go to the home of Ismet Kurbegovic, which was close by; while the men were ordered to form a column of two by two, to go in a direction which was unknown to us at the time and to go with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you where you were supposed to go?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. After we stopped a bit, they told us they are taking us to the bridge of Vrhpolje, where allegedly -- supposedly a bus would be waiting for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you were taken towards the Vrhpolje bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Twenty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still remember the names of these people and the age of these people?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and state names which you remember and their age.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll -- by the order of Ceric Miralem, approximately 70 years of age; Ceric Enver, who was at the time 38 years of age, maybe 40; Ceric Midhat, 32, 33 years of age; Begic Nail, 65; Begic Muhamed, 68; Begic Fuad, 27; Begic Elmedin, 18 years; Begic Irfan, 25 years of age; Begic Munib, 26; then myself, who -- I was 24 years at that time; Begic Nedzad, who was 18, 19; Dizdarevic Ismet, who was 52; Dizdarevic Muhamed, 23; Dizdarevic Mirsad, 17; Dizdarevic Enes, 15 years of age; Begic Muharem, 23; Begic Hakija, 57; and Kurbegovic Ismet, 40, 42.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I would like to show the witness a map, which is called Hrustovo-Vrhpolje overview. And it will be the Prosecutor's Exhibit P803. And we will distribute it immediately. If we could place it on the ELMO. And I would like to ask the witness if he could take a highlighter and draw by himself the road from Begici towards the Vrhpolje bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we will talk in details what happened during the road -- during the way.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can now only briefly comment the road towards the Vrhpolje bridge. Where did they stop? Where did they -- where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Immediately after coming out of the village, some -- a few hundred yards, there was a weekend cottage there. And at a point when we stopped, next to us there was a bigger unit that was resting. And there they asked our escorts to shoot us immediately on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will stop you here, because I didn't ask you the question who was in charge of this column? Who was in charge to take you to the Vrhpolje bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: The lieutenant that was commander of that unit ordered Jadranko Palija to take us to the bridge together with seven armed soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we can proceed with your road. You stated that shortly after you left Begici you were stopped with other soldiers, and you stated that they wanted to kill you and Jadranko stopped them. What happened after this?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: After that briefly stopping, we continued a column of two abreast up to the elevation of Vinogradina and then we proceeded towards the hamlet Hrustovacka Stanica, right here. Along the way, we were told that if anybody from that elevation of Hrustovo-Vrhpolje will be shooting, that they would kill us or we would be killed also in case we tried to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you reach this point. What happened after you reach this particular point?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: When we arrived to Hrustovacka Stanica, we passed a bridge over the river of Sanica. After crossing this bridge, we found a slaughterhouse which was used by a butcher shop, here on the picture. We continued. We didn't stop there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record -- one moment, sir. Just for the record, the Chamber notes that the witness indicated the photo number 3 with the words "butcher's shop" underneath, as it appears on -- tendered Exhibit P803. You may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may proceed. What happened when you crossed this little bridge over the Sanica River?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: We were continuing in a column of two abreast. It -- we were walking along the left side of the road. And in this column Ceric Miralem for whom it was too fast -- we walked too fast for him, he had breathing problems. He son Enes helped him, he was leaning on his son. And then the soldier Jadranko Palija took out these two persons and took them into the slaughter shed. Before entering that -- the slaughter establishment, I saw that he was taking out his pistol and that he was entering the premises of the slaughter -- slaughtering establishment. I heard a shot -- a very loud shot. After that he came out of the butcher shop and he put back his pistol in the holster, and he continued to walk with the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen these two people again?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Enes Ceric was?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Enes Ceric worked in the public prosecutor's office in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After taking away Miralem and Enes Ceric, did you proceed towards the Vrhpolje bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: We didn't even stop. We continued along this -- with the same pace towards that bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: After coming out to the main road Sanski Most-Kljuc, and the road which leads to Hrustovo and Vrhpolje, there Jadranko Palija called out Kurbegovic Ismet from the column. He called him out at the stop sign traffic sign, and asked him for the last time taking out his pistol and aiming at him to admit where the sniper rifle is. Ismet said that he had no sniper weapon, and I saw when Jadranko shot him at a distance from 1 metre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he dead?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to use as evidence a photo which would be Prosecutor's Exhibit P804. And it is a picture of the Vrhpolje bridge with the roads coming from Hrustovo. And this picture was taken in the year 2001 by the Prosecutor of the team 1. And we will distribute it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, now, your column is coming closer to the Vrhpolje Bridge. Is -- can you see on this photo the place where Ismet Kurbegovic was shot, or is it still too -- too far away?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No. He was shot on the road -- along the road -- at the stop sign, which was at the crossroads right there. And he remained lying -- he lay there while we continued our march towards the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what further happened during your march to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: We continued in a column, two abreast, along the left side of the road. And right in front, some 50, 60 metres in front of the bridge, from Kljuc a military van passed and Jadranko Palija got in on the seat by the driver. Then riding along -- parallel with the column, he asked Irfan Begic to get out of the column, and then Jadranko Palija shot him from that vehicle. As the vehicle was moving -- when it was moving, I could see the lower part of Irfan's body, which was then rolling down along this embankment. After that, we arrived to the bridge --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, now I would like to stop you, and I want to play the video. And we will manage the video exactly before the break. It's a video which has already been exhibited. It's P447?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And I would like to ask the technicians to start the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Begic, if you would be so kind and comment what you will see on the screen when we have the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When Madam Richterova tells you if you would like to comment, it means that if you need us to freeze at any one moment the picture that you are seeing on the screen, on the monitor, you must tell us, because otherwise we don't know. I mean, if you want us to stop so that you indicate something to us, that's how you have to do it. Okay? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It's still the bridge part. Excuse me. The video is still not on. Sorry. Sorry. It's my fault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what do we see on the video now?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: On this video, you can see the bridge from the point where we came from Hrustovo, that is, extreme right, you can see the crossroads where Ismet Kurbegovic was shot dead. And then you can see that stretch up to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. A bit back. Stop. Here I would like to show you exactly where Irfan Begic was shot, where he was killed. It's here at the very end, on the right, the extreme right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We can move on with the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we pause here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which road did you arrive at this point? Was it from the bottom of the screen, the road which is coming from the bottom of the screen or the upper side?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. We came by the road at the bottom of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We can move on, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the village?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Vrhpolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is the road you --

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the village in the distance is? This village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we pause.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the road --

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: This is the road to Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take this road?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was the road which we saw before going down towards the bottom of the screen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We can stop -- we can stop the video now. I only wanted to show the road and the bridge itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Richterova. We will have a 30-minute break. We will resume immediately after, with the understanding that Mr. Ackerman will not be here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the meeting that I was going to attend was cancelled. I hope --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I hope you don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I hope before I announced in open court that I was going to be able to attend it. Anyway, this was cancelled. And Mr. Cayley, of course, thinks this is another technique.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, before you -- before Madam Richterova continues and Madam Richterova, I'm going to be a little bit cryptic, because the witness is here and I don't want to waste time having him leave the room and come in again. Please look at the second full paragraph of his statement to you. Read it, particularly the last sentence of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just so I'm reading the right thing, we're talking about the paragraph that begins "The documents"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Yes. Then may I remind you what I asked from you this morning to have ready, which you did. I have two documents, one is one which has the number 00935078. And I would like you to look at the bottom of that first page and the second page. You'll see what I mean. You have a replication of the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You're being so cryptic I'm not actually following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I mean at the bottom of the first page. What do you have that is replicated? Don't answer me, but you should see it. That's repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I see -- I see four signatures at the bottom of the page that I have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The first page? I see only --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You're now on this page or you're on this page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. No. I am referring to the two new documents that you brought forward that I asked you for this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- Something that is replicated. And it is replicated again at the retro of that page, at the back of that page, and again on the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the other document, which supposedly should be the same, that is, the document which has your number 00431945. This seems to be a document which should have the same replication but it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yeah, we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I am sure that you've brought one document before it was -- before what your witness said he was doing -- what he said he was doing in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We have a copy with replicated signatures. I apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have that straight away, please. Mr. Ackerman and Madam Fauveau, have you followed me? I suppose you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Judge, I'll say yes, because it's probably doesn't make much difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. What I'm ensuring is that now that he's confirmed that he has the right document, what I suspect happened was that when I asked Mr. Cayley to bring forward the originals that he -- that the witness had signed in the presence of -- allegedly in the presence of the other two persons, according to this statement it was shown these witnesses and asked -- these statements and asked to countersign them by the Office of the Prosecutor, which he did according to his statement. And I wanted those to be here now before -- so we can have them photocopied now and distributed, please. I'm just anticipating making sure that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No. Absolutely, Your Honour. In fact on the shorter statement the one of the 18th of April, 1996, there's also a version with one signature. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, fine. And you have the version with two signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Okay. So the only version you require with two signatures is the statement of the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of the 16th of April, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. It should have two signatures by the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What I don't understand is whether we have that document or if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope you have. I'm making sure that you get it now. In fact, what I'm -- what I'm making sure is that this document is made available now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's the same one that I was using last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It may not be, because I don't recall that the one you were using last week had a double signature by Mr. Begic. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't recall -- I don't recall either. I don't think it did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I don't think it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I notice that in his statement he says, "I have now endorsed each page of these copies which are attached to the statement with my signature." So I expect to have -- I expected to have and I am having now a copy of his statements to you know who with a double signature, the original and the countersignature, and that's what I'm making sure of.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It may be that the Prosecution believes that those were given to us and in fact they may have been. I don't know. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But it doesn't help. If I don't have it, I don't have it. There's not much I can do about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just trying to be helpful, so as not to avoid problems. Yes, Madam Fauveau. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The copies that I have I think are the same as those of Mr. Ackerman's, and they do indeed have the signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you. So I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just to confirm, Your Honour, it was disclosed, the one with the double signatures, to the Defence on the 14th of December of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the year 2000. So you had it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Madam Richterova, you may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, before the adjournment you told us that your group reached the Vrhpolje Bridge. Who was at that time at the Vrhpolje Bridge, if anybody?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: There were a lot of soldiers at the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that they were Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I knew many of them, and they wore the same uniforms with insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom did you recognise among these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I recognised Marinko Acimovic, Nenad ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you cannot remember his name, it's enough when you state only the first name. Whom else did you know?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Predrag Vujinovic, Zivkovic, I also recognised Simic. Also present was a man in civilian clothes who drove the ambulance, and his name was Vujinovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We understand that it happened many years ago, so you do not remember exact names. You were at the bridge. There were your group and the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I remembered. Nenad Kaurin was one of them. Kaurin was his surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will repeat the question before you -- which I said before you stated the name. There was your group of people from Begici and the soldiers. What happened at the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: When we reached the bridge, they ordered us to line up against the fence, against the railing, upstream in relation to the river, one by one. And then they ordered us to take off our clothes and our shoes for them to search us. That is what we did. And they searched us by hitting individuals with truncheons during the search. After that, a soldier asked us whether we could dive well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, we will talk about this in details. I would -- I want to return for a second to the moment when you reached the bridge. Did any of the soldiers make any speech to you?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't say --

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: They didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't say anything when you reached the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: The moment before they started executing people, Nenad Kaurin said that that day they had to kill 70 Bosniaks because seven Serb soldiers had been killed in the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I interrupted you, you said that one of the soldiers asked who can jump well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after this moment?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Then the soldier Acimovic, first name Marinko pointed his finger at Midhat Ceric, that is, the brother of the two killed previously, Enes Ceric's brother and the son of Miralem, who was the first looking from the right to the left, and he said that he knew that Midho could jump very nicely into the water. Then Jadranko Palija told him to jump into the water, and Midhat jumped. He passed through the fence and jumped on the side of the bridge upstream. At that very moment, four soldiers -- Marinko Acimovic was one of them, as was Nenad Kaurin and another two, whose names I will remember in a moment, were standing at the other side of the fence and waited for Midhat to appear swimming under the bridge. He was swimming. We could hear him swimming. And then the four of them as he appeared open fire at him. And we saw this. I saw the body as the water carried it downstream.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You still have the photo on the ELMO. Can you point at the photo where did you stand and where were the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were standing from this point to this point here on this stretch, and the soldiers were standing on the other side of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it correct to say that the river is going from the left-hand side to the right?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the soldiers started shooting at Midhat Ceric and you saw that they hit the body.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Midhat Ceric jumped to the river, what happened further?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Then this same soldier, Nenad, said, "Next." The man after Midhat was Munib Begic, who was at the time 26 years old. He tried to say something, but they prevented him from doing so by hitting him on the head and they ordered him to jump. Munib did so. He jumped in the same way, and he was also passing under the bridge when these four soldiers shot at him in the same way. I saw that body too flowing down the river. After that, the next in line was Enes Dizdarevic, who was 15 years old, one of three sons who were there with their father. He was also ordered to jump in the same way. He did so. He tried to do so without a second thought by squeezing himself through the iron railing on the bridge. At that moment the soldier Jadranko Palija came up to him and shot at him with his pistol from close range. This body fell into the water. And as it passed under the bridge, those four men shot at it in the same way as before. The killing continued in this same order. The next was his older brother Mirsad Dizdarevic, 17 years old, who was also allowed to jump and who was killed in the same way. After his killing, some other soldiers came up, who to the right of the bridge -- who were standing to the right of the bridge and all of them started beating all those who were still standing on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also beaten?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just then there was one left in front of me, Elmedin Begic. But the moment they started beating all of those captured, I didn't see whether his killing occurred before my turn came or after me. I didn't see his killing with my own eyes. After beating us on the bridge -- in the middle of the bridge, not next to the fence -- then Nenad ordered me and he put his automatic rifle into my mouth. Another soldier ordered him not to shoot there so as to -- not to soil the bridge, but he told him that I should jump into the water as well, and I did so without thinking about it. I just jumped head down, and I was also injured in the process quite seriously. I stood under the bridge because the water was up to my chest there. I had no way out, so I knew -- because I knew I had to pass by and expose myself to the shooting. As I was standing under the bridge, the dirty -- the water was dirtied as I hit it, so I took the opportunity of taking off my white T-shirt, which I was still wearing, and I pushed it deep underwater with my foot and let it flow downstream. When it appeared, they would automatically shoot at it. And I took advantage of this to dive underwater, and I saw them shooting at the T-shirt thinking, probably, that it was me. Just then I swam towards the left bank, and then I continued swimming underwater downstream along the left bank, and I managed to do so, and I swam some 100 metres downstream from the bridge under the water, and then I got hold of a branch that was overlooking the river, and they couldn't see me. So from that position, I observed the bridge, where they continued beating or shooting at the others.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure. The word can mean both.

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: As people were jumping into the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you want the witness to repeat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the witness ought to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think we need to clarify it. Mr. Begic, try to follow what I'm going to tell you. You said from -- I got hold -- then I got hold of a branch that was overlooking the river, and they couldn't see me. So from that position, I observed the bridge, where they continued --" and then we are not quite sure whether you said "beating" or "shooting" at the others. What did you actually say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that distance, one could hear the cries and screams of the others that were remaining on the bridge, and one could see the body falling, though I couldn't identify who it was when they shot at him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's actually shooting, not beating that you're referring to here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard the beating from that spot when I dived out of the water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Is that clear enough for everyone? Yes. You may proceed, Madam Richterova. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, how long did you stay in the water?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I was shot at at about 5.00, as -- as I had to take off my watch at the bridge, I couldn't tell how much time had gone by. But it was the dead of night when I decided to get out of the water. It was about 9.00 or 9.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will return to the bridge once again. You stated that they continued shooting. Do you know how many more bodies were forced to jump from the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I saw another five or six bodies that had jumped or were thrown into the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise them?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long the shooting on the bridge lasted?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: After I surfaced, some 20 minutes after that they -- it continued, the shooting and the bodies falling. And also there were interruptions between one who was shot, one person and the next.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, you also mentioned the name Nedzad Begic. Who was Nedzad Begic?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: That's my younger brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to your brother Nedzad?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen him after the shooting on the Vrhpolje bridge?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will return to the river where you were hiding. And you stated that you stayed in the water till approximately 9.00 in the evening. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: My attention was that at -- in the darkness of the night, that I'd get out of the water, out of the river, as it was very cold. I lost a lot of blood. And I intended to drag myself to the first weekend cottages which are to be found along the banks of Sanica and Sana, where Sanica flows into the Sana and to go away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you manage to do it?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No. During those moments when I wanted to get out of the river, it was already night-time. At a certain point I couldn't hold on to that branch any more, and the water was taking me -- dragging me downstream, and I wasn't capable of moving my arms, my legs. I had no more force in me any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: As the level of the river towards the mouth was getting lower, then the water carried me where I would sink and in other areas would take me to the surface, and I'd breathe some air. And I fought in this way about 100 metres in order to hang onto something where I could get my hands on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you manage to get out of the water?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No. After that, I lost consciousness and the river then took me to the mouth of the river and the centre of the river, where I remained unconscious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came around, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: That occurred some two days later. I thought it was really the next day, but later I understood that it was the second day. I opened my eyes when it started raining. My left eye was closed from the wound I had on my head, so that I couldn't open my left eye. I could see a bit with the right eye, although also my right eye was swollen due to the beating, and I couldn't see very well on that eye. I could see that my hands and legs were still in the water and that only my head and the upper part of my body was washed upon a rock in the centre of the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I immediately remembered what had happened and what had happened to me. I tried -- attempted to move to get out, but I didn't feel my arms, my legs. It was all white, soaked. I had a headache after that. On the same -- at the same moment from a bush a snake came out and it stopped, let's say, about a metre in front of me. Out of -- due to that fear, my blood started circulating, and when the snake left I succeeded in getting up on that rock and there I got my bearings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Nowhere. Not far from there there were those three weekend cottages where I planned to go on that first evening, where I thought I would find some clothing or -- and something to eat. So after I regained a bit of strength, I succeeded in getting to one of these weekend cottages. I found a blanket. I also found a hat with a net. It was a hat for the protection against bees. I didn't find any food, so I returned to the same place, where I remained the next few days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to find some people to help you?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: I didn't look out for anybody who could help me. I just looked at the mouth of the river to see whether there would be any survivors along the banks, but I didn't find anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end, did you contact anybody to help you?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: No. Not until Friday morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened Friday morning?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: On Thursday evening, there was a lot of -- the weather was very bad, a storm with rain. And I took the advantage of that to go to a Serb's house, which was next to our house. We were very close with that family. We were friends. And then I tried to reach them and to ask them for help. I took the advantage of the storm, and at midnight I got into the stables, waiting for dawn. And when Zeljko Krlic went out of his house -- came out of his house, I called him. They took me in, not knowing what really happened to us. I asked him whether he knew what happened to my brother, and he said, "Yes. They have all been killed on the bridge." And allegedly, because we were attacking with our bare hands the checkpoint on the bridge. That is what Jadranko Palija stated when he returned after the killings to the hamlet of Begici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in this Serb house?

utterances.speaker: RAJIF BEGIC
utterances.text: Krlic Andja brought some alcohol, with which we cleaned the wound on my hand. We put also some poultice on the places where I was wounded. I put on some dry clothing. I had tea. And due to the fatigue, I fell asleep quite soon. Half an hour later or even less, we could hear -- I could hear voices which were asking that I get out of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to stop here, because I know that my colleague Andrew Cayley has some procedural things to discuss. And I will continue tomorrow, and I will have probably 15 more minutes to complete this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Madam Richterova. Mr. Begic, I thank you. You will be escorted out of the courtroom now and you will return tomorrow morning at 9.00, where you will be -- you will continue your testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, may we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 1.46 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 31st day of May, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 25
